subject: industrial-systems
audience: FE Industrial & Systems candidates and industrial engineering students
title: The Sample Mean That Crossed 53, Even Though 53.5 Looked Safe
featured_title: THE SAMPLE MEAN THAT CROSSED 53 EVEN THOUGH 53.5 LOOKED SAFE

presentation.challenge: The individual-process spread looked wide enough to contain 53.5, but an x̄ chart uses the standard error of the sample mean. The upper control limit was 53.0.

practice.primary_question: How are three-sigma control limits for an x-bar chart calculated when the process standard deviation is known?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using μ±3σ, which describes individual observations, instead of μ±3σ/√n for subgroup means.

case_dna.target_misconception: A subgroup mean of 53.5 is in control because it lies inside the individual three-sigma range 44 to 56.
case_dna.why_plausible: The process mean and standard deviation are correct, but the wrong variability scale is used for subgroup averages.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: With μ=50, σ=2, and n=4, the standard error is 1 and the x-bar limits are 50±3=47 to 53. A subgroup mean of 53.5 is above the UCL.
case_dna.corrected_model: For an x-bar chart with known σ and subgroup size n, use UCL/LCL=μ±3σ/√n.

problem_statement: A stable process has historical mean μ=50.0 mm and known standard deviation σ=2.0 mm. Quality engineers monitor subgroup means using samples of n=4 and three-sigma x-bar limits. A new subgroup has mean 53.5 mm. A note compares 53.5 with μ±3σ=44 to 56 mm and labels the subgroup in control. Determine the correct x-bar control limits and status of the subgroup.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The wrong variability scale was used for the subgroup mean.
gates.prompt: What standard deviation applies to a subgroup mean?

options.label: Use μ±3σ/√n
options.reason: Subgroup means vary with standard error σ/√n.

options.label: Use μ±3σ
options.reason: Those limits correspond to individual observations, not sample means.

options.label: Use μ±3σ/n
options.reason: Standard error divides σ by √n, not n.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Plot the subgroup mean
gates.result: The subgroup mean 53.5 mm is above the 53.0 mm UCL.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the control limits
gates.prompt: Calculate 50+3(2/√4). Enter the UCL in mm.
gates.success: SE=1.0 mm, so LCL=47.0 mm and UCL=53.0 mm.

cards.text: 53.5 mm exceeds the UCL by 0.5 mm, so the point signals special-cause variation.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the control-chart note
report: C1. The process mean is 50 mm.
C2. The process σ is 2 mm.
C3. Since 53.5 is between 44 and 56, the subgroup mean is in control.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This is the stated historical process mean.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated process standard deviation.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It applies individual-observation limits to a subgroup mean.

evidence_choices.label: UCL=50+3(2/√4)=53.0 mm
evidence_choices.reason: This is the correct three-sigma x-bar upper control limit.

correction.template: The x-bar limits are {lcl} to {ucl} mm, and the 53.5 mm subgroup mean is {status}.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Increase subgroup size to nine
gates.constraint: Keep μ=50 mm and σ=2 mm.

options.label: The limits tighten to 48.0 and 52.0 mm
options.reason: σ/√9=0.667, so three standard errors equal 2.0 mm.

options.label: The limits stay at 44 and 56 mm
The limits become 49 and 51 mm
options.reason: That would be tighter than the three-sigma limits for n=9.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Classify another subgroup
gates.prompt: With n=4 and the same process parameters, is x̄=51.8 mm in control?

options.label: Yes, because 51.8 lies between 47 and 53
options.reason: The subgroup mean is within the three-sigma x-bar limits.

options.label: No, because it differs from 50
options.reason: Control does not require every subgroup mean to equal the center line.

options.label: Cannot determine without individual observations
options.reason: The subgroup mean can be compared directly with the stated x-bar limits.

gates.explanation: A subgroup mean inside the established control limits does not trigger a one-point out-of-control signal.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the control-chart calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that subgroup-mean control limits use the standard error σ/√n rather than the standard deviation of individual observations.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Individual-observation limits were used for an x-bar chart.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Sample means have lower variability than individual measurements.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use μ±3σ/√n for the stated x-bar chart.

seo.seo_title: X-Bar Control Limits With Known Sigma | FE Industrial E-087
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Industrial & Systems Case E-087: with μ=50, σ=2, and n=4, x-bar limits are 47 to 53 mm, so x̄=53.5 is out of control.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Industrial x bar control limits known sigma
seo.excerpt: An x-bar chart uses the standard error of subgroup means, not the full standard deviation of individual observations.
seo.direct_answer: For μ=50 mm, σ=2 mm, and n=4, SE=2/√4=1 mm. Three-sigma x-bar limits are 50±3(1), or 47 to 53 mm. A subgroup mean of 53.5 mm is therefore out of control.

faqs.q: What standard deviation is used for an x-bar chart with known sigma?
What happens to x-bar limits as subgroup size increases?
faqs.a: They become narrower because σ/√n decreases.
